prompt:
You maintain a running summary of a long engineering document that is being read part by part, so that a later reader can model the system in SysML v2 without seeing the earlier parts.
Update the summary with the new part. Keep, as compactly as possible: the full names of system elements, actors and items; every alias or call sign with the full name it stands for; which element produces, sends or receives which item; modes and normative requirements. At most 300 words.

Current summary:
Sentinel Vale: EO mission (land/coastal/cryosphere). Ground segment plans, acquires, keeps ops safe, generates/archives products, controlled service access. Outside: spacecraft, launch segment, external user processing. Mission Control Center (alias Bluebell): real-time ops, anomaly response, releases validated commands; owns contact schedule; primary routing policy point; contact = readiness check, live monitoring, post-pass closure; consoles used by Spacecraft Ops Team (console lead declares pass status, authorizes commands via Command Validation Gateway, pauses on telemetry mismatch; telemetry engineer checks quality/loss/latency/continuity; spacecraft systems engineer checks flight rules, records anomaly context). Flight Dynamics Facility (alias Mistral): orbit, maneuvers; visibility/pointing to planning. Payload Processing Facility (alias Forgehouse): processing, calibration, staging; Primary (nominal)/Backup (failover, lower routing preference, routinely tested) Processing Clusters. Network Control System (alias Lantern): routing, station allocations, contact start/end; authoritative WAN state; sends MCC antenna status, link config, timing references, routing readiness before each pass; vets timing alarms before forwarding to Spacecraft Ops Team. Mission Planning System: receives contact booking requests. Command Validation Gateway shall rule-check commands. Telemetry Ingest Service: accepts frames, validates framing/time continuity, records reception metadata; produces Pass Replay Packet post-contact. Orbit Determination Engine: Doppler Residual Report per pass; state updates basis for visibility, maneuver, pointing predictions. Flight Dynamics Team uses tracking/time tags; monitors timing quality. Product Quality Service; Long Term Archive (authoritative; PPC->LTA rate-limited during contacts); User Services Portal. Ground Network Manager (alias Juniper): accountable antenna assignment/availability, site coordination; Antenna Deicing Notice; pins paths before AOS; latency breach triage; consults Cybersecurity Desk (sends Security Exception Ticket) before blocking. Antennas: North/South S-Band (command, low-rate TM; protected routers to MCC); Kiruna/Svalbard X-Band (high-rate TM; dual WAN to PPF); validate time before contact. Payload Calibration Team. Pass reconstruction at contact close merges command history, TM timing, station status, operator logs to verify objectives. Timing: redundant clocks MCC/FDF with holdover; PTP; authenticated NTP. Per-site security monitoring reviewed each shift. Rules: daily cut-off; safety>timeliness>efficiency; X-band rain downgrade; S-band unavailable

New part:
S093: The Mission Control Center coordinates with the Payload Processing Facility when instrument mode changes, data downlink priorities, or reception gaps could affect downstream processing.
S094: The Payload Calibration Team sends the Calibration Patch Bundle after calibration analysis identifies an approved update for payload processing behavior.
S095: Subsystem specialists are not expected to staff every live contact, but they must be reachable during planned critical activities and whenever a console operator declares an off-nominal condition.
S096: Escalation from the Mission Control Center begins with the console lead, moves to the responsible discipline lead, and then reaches mission management when the condition threatens spacecraft safety, contact continuity, or recovery schedule.
S097: The Spacecraft Operations Team and Flight Dynamics Team coordinate closely before orbit-control activities so that command timing, attitude constraints, tracking expectations, and post-burn assessment steps remain consistent.
S098: When telemetry indicates a possible onboard fault, operators preserve the command state, avoid discretionary commanding, and request specialist review before changing spacecraft configuration.
S099: The Mission Planning System receives operational constraints from mission control after anomalies, station outages, or spacecraft configuration changes require adjustment of future contacts or payload activities.
S100: At the end of each shift, the Mission Control Center records unresolved actions, open engineering questions, and expected specialist responses so that the next operations crew can maintain continuity without relying on informal handover.
S101: Mission planning begins when observation requests arrive through the User Services Portal or from internal operations channels at the Mission Control Center.
S102: The Mission Planning System, also called Cedar in this section, is the authoritative tool for assembling candidate observation timelines and associated ground contact activities.
S103: Each request is checked for requester authority, target definition, time sensitivity, acquisition mode, expected data volume, and any handling restrictions before it is admitted to the planning pool.
S104: The User Services Portal records the request state so that external users can distinguish accepted requests from those still awaiting technical review.
S105: The Spacecraft Operations Team reviews late operational requests when they affect spacecraft attitude, thermal margin, stored command capacity, or contact preparation.
S106: The Flight Dynamics Facility provides orbit predictions and visibility assumptions that the planning cycle uses to determine feasible imaging windows and ground contacts.
S107: The Mission Planning System combines request priority, instrument availability, contact opportunities, onboard storage margin, and downlink capacity into a draft activity schedule.

Return JSON {"summary": "..."}.
